title: Seattle is awarded an NFL franchise
description: The NFL granted Seattle its expansion franchise on June 4, setting the stage for the club to begin play in 1976.

title: Football arrives at the Kingdome
description: The expansion {Team} played their first season in the NFC, with Jim Zorn and Steve Largent beginning a partnership that helped define the early club.

title: The first playoff run
description: In Chuck Knox’s first season, Seattle beat Denver and Miami before its breakthrough postseason ended in the AFC Championship Game.

title: No. 12 is retired for the fans
description: Seattle retired the number 12 on December 15 as a tribute to the home crowd and its impact on games.

title: A Kingdome roar changes the rules
description: The NFL briefly introduced an excessive-crowd-noise rule during an era when visiting offenses struggled to communicate inside the Kingdome.

title: The franchise stays in the Northwest
description: Paul Allen’s purchase secured the {Team}’ future in the Pacific Northwest and cleared the way for a new stadium project.

title: A new outdoor home
description: The {Team} opened their new stadium, beginning the venue era that continues today at Lumen Field.

title: Seattle returns to the NFC
description: NFL realignment moved the {Team} from the AFC West to the NFC West, the conference where they had played their inaugural season.

title: The 12 Flag tradition begins
description: Twelve original season-ticket holders raised the 12 Flag before the October 12 home game, launching a lasting pregame ritual.

title: The first NFC crown
description: A 13–3 team powered by Shaun Alexander, Matt Hasselbeck and Walter Jones won the NFC and reached the franchise’s first Super Bowl.

title: Beast Quake shakes Seattle
description: Marshawn Lynch’s 67-yard playoff touchdown against New Orleans sent the stadium crowd into a celebration measured by a nearby seismic station.

title: Defense carries Seattle to the summit
description: The top-seeded {Team} capped a dominant season by winning Super Bowl XLVIII, the first league championship in franchise history.

title: Back-to-back NFC champions
description: Seattle returned to the Super Bowl after winning a second consecutive NFC championship.

title: A second Lombardi Trophy
description: A 14–3 regular season ended with Seattle defeating New England 29–13 in Super Bowl LX for the franchise’s second league championship.
